query: What in the conversation explains why Marcus changed how he manages group pace, and what specifically appeared to cause it?
gold:
Early state (Sessions 1-3): Marcus set a fast pace from the front and expected the group to keep up. There is no mention of rest stops in his route plans for Sessions 1-3; he frames routes by gain and group standard ('manageable by local standards') without contingency for pace variation.

Shift signal (Session 4): Marcus opens the debrief with: 'Going forward I'll build rest stops into the plan and we move at the slowest comfortable speed.' This is an unprompted policy statement, not a response to a request.

Trigger: Priya twisted her ankle on the High Crag descent while trying to keep pace. The incident is described as having forced Marcus to reorganise the rest of the day. Dmitri's assessment confirmed it was 'the pace pressure' not Priya's technique that caused the problem. Marcus internalised this.

Evolved state (Sessions 4 onward): Rest stops appear explicitly in Marcus's route planning ('rest stops at 3km and 6km,' Session 8). The policy holds -- no further pace-related incidents occur, and Bridget's only complaint in Session 4 is that the unplanned stop (not a planned one) caused the overrun.
context:
[1] (about=Marcus, episodic, t6 @2025-10-12T14:07:00) We got her down fine. I've been thinking about the way I've been pacing these days. Moving at the front and expecting the group to match isn't working for everyone. Going forward I'll build rest stops into the plan and we move at the slowest comfortable speed. Let me know by Thursday if anything needs adjusting for next week.
[2] (about=Dmitri, episodic, t6 @2025-10-12T14:22:00) Noted. You read the terrain correctly. The pace pressure was the problem, not your technique.
[3] (about=GROUP, said_by=Marcus, group-interaction, t20 @2025-11-30T14:32:00) Spring schedule to include one overnight per month. Marcus will plan accordingly.
agent_answer: Marcus changed his pacing because he realized that his usual style — moving at the front and expecting the group to match his speed — "isn't working for everyone." So he decided to build rest stops into the plan and move at the slowest comfortable speed. The specific cause appears to be that pace pressure was the problem: Dmitri confirmed that "the pace pressure was the problem, not your technique," supporting Marcus's own reassessment.
